title: How do we draw an angle that is bigger than a straight line?
description: Five angle measures are named by kind first, and four of them are drawn with the protractor scale from zero. The measure that is bigger than one hundred eighty is drawn through the smaller angle that completes the full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: name the kind first to know how wide to draw; a reflex angle is drawn through three hundred sixty take away the measure. Watch for students who say a protractor cannot draw an angle bigger than one hundred eighty.

video_script.why: The child names each measure by kind, draws four with the protractor scale, and draws the reflex one through its smaller partner angle.
video_script.substitution: Compare each of 140, 82, 195, 70 and 35 with 90 and 180, then draw with the scale; for 195 use 360 take away 195 = 165.
video_script.anchor: a base ray with a protractor on it, ready to draw five angles
video_script.payoff_line: The scale draws the first four, and the full turn draws the big one

final_answer.value: each angle drawn with the protractor; 195° drawn through 165°
final_answer.spoken: each angle is drawn with the protractor, and one hundred ninety five is drawn through one hundred sixty five

hold_back: all five angles drawn on base rays
never_show: a claim that 195° cannot be drawn
maths_rules: 140 is more than 90 and less than 180, so it is obtuse
82, 70 and 35 are less than 90, so they are acute
195 is more than 180 and less than 360, so it is reflex
the scale of the protractor stops at 180°
full turn = 360°, so the smaller partner of 195° is 360° − 195° = 165°
video_script.design: One base ray and a protractor. The kind of each measure is shown first as a mark on a 0 to 360 strip. Four angles are drawn from the zero of the scale; the reflex one is drawn as the outside of a 165 degree angle.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about drawing angles.
<bookmark mark='ray'/>We have a base ray and a protractor.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>The measures are one hundred forty, eighty two, one hundred ninety five, seventy and thirty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How will we draw all five?

beats.on_screen: the base ray and the cards hold still on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a protractor on a base ray with its centre on the end point; the scale runs from 0° to 180° and its end is marked; a full circle is drawn beside it

marks.centre: the centre of the protractor sits on the end point of the base ray
marks.scale: the scale is lit from 0° on the base ray to 180°
marks.end: the end of the scale at 180° is marked, with a full circle beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>To draw an angle, put the centre of the protractor on the end of the base ray.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>The scale starts at zero on the base ray.
<bookmark mark='end'/>It stops at one hundred eighty, but a full turn is three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five angle measures to draw.

beats.on_screen: To find: a drawing of each angle

marks.find: the words a drawing of each angle are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to draw an angle of each measure.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: compare with 90° and 180°: 140° obtuse; 82°, 70°, 35° acute; 195° reflex

marks.obtuse: 140° is placed between 90° and 180° on a strip and labelled obtuse
marks.acute: 82°, 70° and 35° are placed before 90° and labelled acute
marks.reflex: 195° is placed past 180° and labelled reflex

beats.colours: acute = teal, obtuse = amber, reflex = rose
narration: <bookmark mark='obtuse'/>Step one, compare each measure with ninety and one hundred eighty.
One hundred forty is obtuse.
<bookmark mark='acute'/>Eighty two, seventy and thirty five are acute.
<bookmark mark='reflex'/>One hundred ninety five is past one hundred eighty, so it is reflex.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: for 140°, 82°, 70° and 35°, mark the measure on the scale from 0° and join it to the vertex

marks.mark: a dot is put on the scale at each measure, counting from 0° on the base ray
marks.join: each dot is joined to the vertex and an arc is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='mark'/>Step two, four of the measures fit on the scale.
Count from zero on the base ray, and put a dot at the measure.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Join the dot to the vertex, and draw the arc.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 195° is past the scale, so take it from the full turn: 360° − 195° = 165°

marks.past: 195° is shown past the end of the scale
marks.take: 195° is taken away from the full turn 360° and 165° is left
marks.left: 165° is written as what is left

narration: <bookmark mark='past'/>Step three, one hundred ninety five is past the end of the scale.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take it away from the full turn, because what is left is the smaller partner angle.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Three hundred sixty take away one hundred ninety five leaves one hundred sixty five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: draw 165° on the scale, then mark the angle on the other side, the long way round

marks.small: an angle of 165° is drawn with the scale
marks.outside: the arc is drawn on the outside, the long way round, in rose

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step four, draw an angle of one hundred sixty five degrees with the scale.
<bookmark mark='outside'/>Then mark the angle on the other side, the long way round.
That outside angle is the reflex angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check: read each drawn angle again; 165° + 195° = 360°

marks.read: the protractor is laid on each finished angle and gives the same measure
marks.full: the 165° and 195° angles are added and fill the full circle

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step five, put the answer back in the question.
Read each finished angle again with the protractor.
<bookmark mark='full'/>For the big one, the two sides must fill a full turn.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 140°, 82°, 70°, 35° drawn on the scale; 195° drawn through 165°
